claim_summary: ChatAD contributes multi-agent time-series instruction evolution and its training data, reasoning-focused SFT and TKTO model optimization, and an anomaly-detection evaluation benchmark with cross-task tests.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose TSEvol, an LLM-driven agentbased time series evolution algorithm for SFT instruction synthesis.
We develop TKTO (Time Series Kahneman-Tversky Optimization), a reinforcement learning approach designed to refine ChatAD.
We establish LLADBench to evaluate the ChatAD against nine state-of-the-art baselines.

modules.name: Multi-agent temporal instruction evolution
modules.scope_reason: R2 places this on the LLM side because the multi-agent procedure synthesizes time-series instruction supervision for SFT rather than serving as an inference harness. R3 does not apply to this model-side module.

evidence.quote: TSEvol consists of (a) TS Instruction Evolution Pool, (b) Cognitive Reasoning Layer, and (c) Interactive Feedback-driven Layer.
The Supervisor evaluates the quality of each evolution loop (a complete Q&A pair) and provides implicit feedback to guide subsequent question generation.

modules.name: TSEData-20K dialogue and reasoning dataset
modules.scope_reason: R2 places this contributed dataset on the LLM side because it supplies multi-turn anomaly-detection instruction data used to train ChatAD. R3 does not apply to this model-side module.
rubric_path: R1:contributed dataset built for the LLM

evidence.quote: We present the first LAD reasoning and multiturn dialogue dataset TSEData-20K using TSEvol, comprising 10011 high-quality anomaly detection dialogues
we propose a two-stage training paradigm for ChatAD: initial SFT for AD task using TSEData, followed by TKTO optimization

modules.name: LoRA supervised fine-tuning for anomaly detection
modules.scope_reason: R2 places LoRA SFT on the LLM side because it updates the model adapter to produce anomaly-detection responses. R3 does not apply to this model-side module.

evidence.quote: We adopt LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) (Hu et al., 2022)-based SFT to train the adapter.
we contribute three models using TSED-20K as shown in Table 1

modules.name: Time-series Kahneman-Tversky preference optimization
modules.scope_reason: R2 places TKTO on the LLM side because it optimizes ChatAD model parameters using scored outputs. R3 does not apply to this model-side module.

evidence.quote: We propose TKTO, which leverages TS features to boost ChatAD’s cross-task generalization performance.
To quantify the quality of each pair, we define a preference vector d = [d0 , d1 , d2 , d3 ]

modules.name: LLADBench task evaluation benchmark
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the benchmark's core logic embeds task-specific output parsing and metrics for anomaly detection, forecasting, imputation, classification, and reasoning; its evaluators and criteria must be redesigned when those task semantics change. The temporal data being evaluated does not make this a GTS mechanism because the module is bound to task objectives, and it is not GH because it is an evaluation resource rather than task-independent execution management.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - task outputs and criteria are embedded; changing task semantics requires redesign
R7:anomaly detection, forecasting, classification, imputation, and QA

evidence.quote: LLADBench consists of four tasks. To evaluate single-turn and multi-turn dialogue capability, we employ Accuracy (Acc), F1 score, and False Positive Rate (FPR).
The proposed LLADBench includes a series of automated result analysis scripts.

task_performance.quote: For the forecasting and imputation tasks, the numerical prediction performance consistently outperforms the benchmarks.

reconciliation.reason: The card's TSEvol module is supported as a contributed multi-agent procedure that evolves time-series instruction data for SFT; it remains an LLM-side training-data mechanism.

TKTO added as a distinct model-training module
reconciliation.reason: The paper describes a two-stage pipeline: SFT trains ChatAD on TSEData and TKTO is a separate preference optimization that refines ChatAD for cross-task generalization.

notes: The paper separately contributes TSEvol, its TSEData-20K output dataset, ChatAD SFT, TKTO, and LLADBench. Task-performance evidence includes anomaly detection, reasoning, and cross-task results; the packet does not report explicit chronology/leakage validity or measured downstream decision utility.
